title: Design an In-Memory Key-Value Store
relevance: High — systems-flavored LLD / machine-coding staple (campus + experienced); Lyft, Uber, Coinbase, Anchorage, Amazon, Google, Meta, Atlassian, and Flipkart-style loops probe get/set/delete, TTL, nested or MULTI-style transactions, CAS, eviction Strategy, and concurrency.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad machine-coding often wants HashMap store + TTL or KV + nested transactions with concurrency and data-structure design. Experienced/SDE-2+ rounds harden on optimistic vs nested txn, conditional remove races, striped locks, capacity eviction Strategy, injectable clock, and persistence stretch (Lyft/Uber/Coinbase-style txn DB; Amazon/Meta/Google systems LLD). Sibling rounds: lq13_cache_lld (eviction), hq14_distributed_cache / ByteByteGo KV (distributed HLD), h03_caching. High-frequency infra OOP staple alongside rate limiter, logger, and LRU cache.

phases.goal: Lock functional/non-functional scope: core map ops, optional TTL/txn/CAS/eviction, and single-process in-memory assumptions.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: get(key), set(key, value), delete(key) with O(1) average; miss returns null / empty.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists get/set/delete first and states average O(1) lookup/update without scanning the map.

must_hit.point: Ask about common extensions: per-key TTL, capacity + eviction, nested transactions or MULTI/EXEC/DISCARD, compareAndSet, exists/ttl, typed values.
must_hit.evidence_hint: They explicitly ask the interviewer which of TTL, capacity, txn shape, and CAS are in scope before coding.

must_hit.point: NFR: thread-safe concurrent clients, no stale reads of expired keys, extensible eviction/storage, injectable Clock for tests, bounded memory if capacity set.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions thread-safety, expired-key correctness, and deterministic Clock injection alongside memory bounds.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: single JVM/process in-memory unless told otherwise; no disk durability unless asked; HLD sharding/replication is stretch only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Clarifies single-process LLD vs distributed Dynamo/Redis Cluster and keeps durability out unless prompted.

probes: Which features are in scope—TTL, capacity eviction, nested begin/commit/abort, or Redis MULTI/WATCH—and is this single-process only?

hints.1: Start by listing mandatory ops versus optional extensions before sketching classes.
hints.2: Separate FR (get/set/delete + asked extensions) from NFR (thread-safety, expiry freshness, extensibility, Clock).
hints.3: Mandatory: O(1) get/set/delete; ask TTL, capacity, nested txn or MULTI, CAS; assume single-process in-memory, no durability unless asked.

phases.goal: Name the core objects: facade store, storage map, entry metadata, optional txn manager, eviction policy, clock/sweeper.

must_hit.point: KeyValueStore / InMemoryDB is the facade over Storage (map) holding Entry / VersionedValue.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws a store facade that delegates to a Storage map of entries rather than dumping logic in one class.

must_hit.point: Entry holds value plus optional absolute expireAt and optional version for optimistic txn/CAS.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Entry fields include value, expireAtMs (or none), and version—not just a bare string value.

must_hit.point: Optional Transaction / TransactionManager owns isolation (nested stack or writeSet/readSet/deleteSet).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions a txn manager or transaction object separate from the map for begin/commit/abort or MULTI.

must_hit.point: Optional EvictionPolicy Strategy, Clock, and ExpirySweeper for capacity and active TTL.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names eviction policy, injectable clock, and a background sweeper as optional collaborators.

probes: What objects own the value metadata, transaction isolation, and eviction victim selection?

hints.1: Think facade store, map storage, and an entry that carries more than the raw value.
hints.2: Split Entry (value/version/expireAt), optional TransactionManager, and EvictionPolicy/Clock/Sweeper.
hints.3: KeyValueStore facade → Storage of Entry/VersionedValue; optional TransactionManager, EvictionPolicy, Clock, ExpirySweeper.

phases.goal: Show interfaces and relationships: Facade, Storage, EvictionPolicy, Entry, Transaction shapes.

must_hit.point: KeyValueStore facade validates, lazy-expires, delegates to Storage, notifies EvictionPolicy, enforces capacity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes the request path through the facade: validate → expire check → storage → policy/capacity.

must_hit.point: Storage interface with HashMapStorage / ConcurrentMapStorage; EvictionPolicy interface with LRU/LFU/FIFO/NoEviction.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows Storage and EvictionPolicy as interfaces with concrete strategies, not hard-wired types inside the facade.

must_hit.point: Transaction either nested stack frame Map<key,(newVal,oldVal)> or optimistic writeSet/deleteSet plus readSet of versions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks one txn model and sketches either delta frames or readSet/writeSet/deleteSet on the Transaction type.

must_hit.point: EvictionPolicy hooks: onAccess/onPut/onRemove and evictCandidate(); DIP inject Storage, EvictionPolicy, Clock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Policy methods update on map events and return a victim; constructors take injected dependencies, not a Singleton.

probes: Sketch the class diagram—where do Facade, Storage, Entry, TransactionManager, and EvictionPolicy sit?

hints.1: Prefer interfaces for storage and eviction behind a single KeyValueStore API.
hints.2: Facade orchestrates; Storage holds Entry; TransactionManager optional; EvictionPolicy returns victims.
hints.3: KeyValueStore → Storage + optional EvictionPolicy/TransactionManager/ExpirySweeper/Clock; Entry has value, version, expireAtMs.

phases.goal: Implement O(1) map ops, Redis-style TTL, and either nested delta transactions or optimistic versioned commit, plus CAS.

must_hit.point: Default data plane: ConcurrentHashMap of Entry for O(1) average get/set/delete.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses ConcurrentHashMap<K,Entry> (or equivalent) and keeps hot path average O(1), not a full-map scan on get.

must_hit.point: TTL lazy/passive: on access if now >= expireAt, delete and return miss; prefer absolute expireAt on the entry.
must_hit.evidence_hint: get/set path checks absolute deadline and removes expired entries before returning a value.

must_hit.point: Active expiry samples keys periodically so cold expired keys do not leak memory (Redis-style; sample work O(sample) not full sweep).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds a sweeper/sampler for TTL keys and contrasts it with lazy-only leakage on never-read keys.

must_hit.point: Nested delta stack: begin pushes change-log; abort restores; nested commit merges to parent; space O(keys touched) not full DB copy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements begin/commit/abort with a delta log sized to touched keys, rejecting whole-map snapshots.

must_hit.point: Optimistic/WATCH shape: buffer writes, track versions in readSet; commit aborts if any read version changed, else apply atomically.
must_hit.evidence_hint: On commit/EXEC, validates versions then applies writeSet/deleteSet or aborts on conflict.

must_hit.point: CAS via compareAndSet(key, expected, new) or version check for set-if-unchanged without a global lock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows atomic replace/version check returning boolean success/failure for concurrent updates.

probes: How do get/set honor TTL, and how do you implement nested begin/commit/abort or optimistic commit without copying the whole map?

hints.1: Map + Entry with expireAt covers the happy path; transactions are either a delta stack or versioned buffers.
hints.2: Lazy expire on access; optional active sampler; txn = O(keys touched) deltas or validate-on-commit versions.
hints.3: ConcurrentHashMap of Entry; lazy delete when now >= expireAt; nested change-log or readSet/writeSet validate-on-commit; CAS/version replace.

phases.goal: Show OCP/DIP via Strategy/Factory/Command so new eviction, storage, or MULTI queuing does not rewrite call sites.

must_hit.point: Strategy: swap LRU/LFU/FIFO/TTL-only eviction or HashMap vs custom table storage behind interfaces.
must_hit.evidence_hint: New eviction or storage is a new class implementing the policy/storage interface.

must_hit.point: Factory builds store from config (capacity, policy, TTL defaults); Facade exposes get/set/delete/expire.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Config-driven factory constructs the facade with chosen capacity/policy rather than hard-coding one setup.

must_hit.point: OCP: add LFU tomorrow via new EvictionPolicy + Factory branch with zero edits to get/set call sites; Command queues MULTI ops / undo on abort.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains adding LFU without touching callers, and optionally Command for queued MULTI/undo.

must_hit.point: Avoid cargo-cult Singleton; prefer DI for Storage, EvictionPolicy, and Clock.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects global Singleton store in favor of injected collaborators for testability.

probes: How would you add LFU eviction tomorrow without changing every get/set call site?

hints.1: Eviction and storage should be pluggable, not baked into the facade.
hints.2: Strategy + Factory + DIP: new policy class and factory branch; inject Clock/Storage.
hints.3: New EvictionPolicy implementation + Factory config; Facade/Storage call sites unchanged; prefer DI over Singleton.

phases.goal: Make single-key ops and compound/txn apply correct under concurrent clients without over-locking.

must_hit.point: Single-key ops use ConcurrentHashMap methods / per-key lock; pair with compute/remove(k,v) for atomic check-and-set.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses map atomics or per-key locking for get/set/delete/CAS rather than only unsynchronized HashMap.

must_hit.point: Compound ops (RMW, txn apply, evict-then-put) need one critical section or CAS retry—never check-then-act without atomicity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Identifies multi-step map sequences and wraps them in a lock/CAS loop instead of separate check then act.

must_hit.point: Prefer striped / per-key locks over one global synchronized on the facade under load; Redis single-threaded command loop is an alternative model.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts global lock demos with striped locks or a single-threaded apply loop under contention.

must_hit.point: ExpirySweeper must use conditional remove(key, expectedEntry)/CAS so it never deletes a fresher entry that replaced an expired one.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sweeper removal is conditional on the exact expired Entry instance, not blind remove(key).

probes: Two threads CAS the same key—how do you ensure only one succeeds, and how does the sweeper avoid deleting a just-refreshed key?

hints.1: Separate single-key map atomics from multi-step critical sections.
hints.2: Use ConcurrentHashMap/CAS for one key; lock or validate for txn apply; conditional remove in the sweeper.
hints.3: Map atomics or per-key locks for single ops; critical section/CAS retry for compound/txn; remove(key, expectedEntry) in the sweeper; mention striped locks or Redis single-thread loop.

tradeoffs.topic: Full snapshot vs delta stack for transactions
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Copying the whole map per begin is simple but O(n) memory; a delta log is O(keys touched) and is the expected Hello Interview answer—abort restores previous values, nested commit merges into the parent.

Lazy alone leaks memory on write-heavy never-read keys; active sampling deletes expired cold keys without a huge per-key timer heap (Redis model). A min-heap of expiries is more exact but costlier under churn.

tradeoffs.topic: Global lock vs ConcurrentHashMap / per-key lock
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Global synchronized is correct for demos; seniors want map atomics plus narrow critical sections for compound ops and txn apply, preferring striped/per-key locks over one facade lock under load.
Optimistic versions/WATCH maximize concurrency and retry on conflict; pessimistic locks keys for the txn duration—simpler reasoning but worse under contention.
Partitioning, replication, and quorum are HLD (hq14 / ByteByteGo); mention as stretch and stay on classes unless prompted—do not build Dynamo mid-LLD.

gotchas.trap: Nested transaction abort undoes outer levels or loses inner commits incorrectly.
gotchas.correction: Inner commit merges child deltas into the parent; abort restores previous values only for the popped frame.

gotchas.trap: Two threads both appear to succeed on CAS.
gotchas.correction: Use a version check or replace(key, oldEntry, newEntry) / compareAndSet so only one atomic update wins.

gotchas.trap: Expired keys remain in memory forever with lazy-only expiry.
gotchas.correction: Add active expiry sampling; lazy alone is insufficient for cold keys.

gotchas.trap: Sweeper deletes a key that was just refreshed with a new value/TTL.
gotchas.correction: Use conditional remove(key, expectedEntry) / CAS, not blind remove(key).

gotchas.trap: Adding LFU requires editing get/set call sites.
gotchas.correction: New EvictionPolicy class plus Factory branch; zero edits to get/set callers (OCP); detail in lq13.

gotchas.trap: Treating the round as pure LeetCode LRU / DLL surgery.
gotchas.correction: Draw the store facade, TTL, and concurrency story; reuse LRU as an EvictionPolicy Strategy, do not stop at the linked-list.

gotchas.trap: Assuming Redis MULTI rolls back like SQL on mid-EXEC failure.
gotchas.correction: Queued commands run atomically; a failed command mid-EXEC does not undo siblings; WATCH provides optimistic abort before EXEC.

gotchas.trap: Jumping to multi-node durability/cluster in the LLD.
gotchas.correction: AOF/snapshot and consistent hashing / Redis Cluster are stretch; hand off to hq14 / ByteByteGo unless asked.
